bull_bear.body: Dividend increased 50% from INR 11 to INR 16.5 per share (sustainable quarterly payout); excess cash returned to shareholders while retaining flexibility for value-accretive bolt-on acquisitions.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Continued secular decline in ILD A2P SMS volumes; Slow adoption rate of new channels (RCS/WhatsApp) relative to competitor pace; Integration complexity of Proximus group synergies; Macro pressure on enterprise discretionary spend.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Candid on past headwinds (AIT cleanup, ILD decline) but highly confident in structural reset; Emphasis on 'live program' execution rather than theoretical strategy; Disciplined capital allocator focused on quality of earnings over sheer scale.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Network API revenue (Silent Verification, SIM swap) is currently booked under legacy SMS segment, masking the true growth rate of the 'New Product' transition; The 'India as Innovation Hub' allows for rapid prototyping (e.g., Aakash deal in months) that is then distributed globally via Proximus, a unique arbitrage not available to standalone peers.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Board proposed ₹2 per share final dividend.
- ₹13,887 mn cash as on 31 March 2026.
- 110% CFO / EBITDA conversion in FY25-26 (cash-flow slide shows CFO/EBITDA of 110.5% in FY 25-26 vs 114.9% in FY 24-25).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Network of 1000+ connected operators allowing SMS termination in any part of the world with the best routing; 280+ direct MNO connects and 900+ MNO connections across the Proximus Global combine
- Full-stack omnichannel CPaaS platform bringing messaging, voice, email and emerging digital channels into a single integrated ecosystem, so enterprises manage customer journeys through one integration
- Carrier-grade, resilient global infrastructure with 20+ global data centers delivering APIs at enterprise scale
- Membership of Proximus Global alongside BICS and Telesign, adding global carrier connectivity, digital identity and fraud prevention, and enabling cross-selling across Europe and North America
- Route Mobile serves as the innovation engine for Proximus Global, with innovations built by its teams deployed across global markets
- Scale and stickiness of enterprise relationships: 3,100+ clients served and 174.9 Bn billable transactions processed in FY 2025-26
- Security and compliance embedded across the platform through stringent governance and global compliance standards, plus regulatory expertise across jurisdictions
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Data privacy and regulatory compliance — BRSR material-issues table flags that processing data exposes the Company to privacy breach claims, and that regulators such as TRAI define the rules for CPaaS players so changes to regulatory requirements could affect business potential; negative implication includes claims under privacy laws and the cost of hiring privacy professionals across jurisdictions. Mitigated via privacy policy, employee training, a compliance programme and audits.
- Cybersecurity threats — Increasing cyber threats can compromise data and operations, with potential financial loss from data breaches and recovery costs; mitigated by advanced cybersecurity tooling, regular security audits and employee training.
- Business continuity / platform downtime — Any downtime can result in poor customer experience and potential customer loss; mitigated with business continuity plans, regular drills and testing, and backup systems. Platform reliability is separately identified as the source of differentiation through high service delivery, requiring infrastructure strengthening, redundancy and continuous monitoring.
- Supply chain disruption across MNOs and infrastructure vendors — Global events can disrupt the supply chain; any disruption in telecom partner operations or hardware vendors affects the ability to deliver quality services, causing delays and increased costs. Mitigated by diversifying the supplier pool and the network of operator connects.
- Technological obsolescence — Rapid technology change can render current systems obsolete, driving increased investment in technology updates; mitigated by regular tech refresh, R&D investment and staying ahead of industry developments.
- Regulatory change across jurisdictions — New regulations can impose additional compliance requirements and costs, and inadvertent violation can create liability; mitigated by tracking regulatory changes and adjusting compliance programmes.
- Talent retention in a niche skill pool — Flagged as both opportunity and risk: revenue depends on a cutting-edge technology talent pool, and the Company may lose in talent retention if the millennial talent pool is not offered satisfactory career programmes and industry-competitive workplace facilities. Mitigation is talent re-skilling and attrition management.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Legacy A2P SMS (ILD) declined structurally but stabilized in Q4; now ~25-33% of revenue mix. New Products (RCS/WhatsApp/Omnichannel) grew 43% CAGR (FY22-26) but slowed to 11% YoY in FY26, constituting ~8% of revenue. MNO Solutions (Firewall/Network APIs) excluded from 'New Products' metric, growing fast with record revenue in Firewall, driven by operator fraud prevention needs.

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Described as an industry-leading global CPaaS platform offering a scalable and flexible omnichannel CPaaS platform to enterprises across industry verticals, globally.
- Third-party recognition cited: "Visionary in Magic Quadrant for CPaaS 2025 - Gartner", "Key Vendor in four Hype Cycle Reports - Gartner" and "Top Tier 1 A2P SMS vendor" - Rocco.
- Network moat framed as 280+ direct MNO connects with overall access to 900+ MNOs (Super Network), plus a global footprint across 20+ locations.
- Customer base described as diverse, with FY 25-26 revenue contribution from select industries listed as Ecommerce 15%, FinServ 11%, Digital native 9%, Telecom & allied Services 7%, Retail, Travel & Hospitality 6%, Tier 1 CPaaS partners 2%.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Client concentration] Top 5 / Top 10 / Top 50 client concentration shown across FY 22-23 to FY 25-26 as 38%/32%/33%/33%, 48%/44%/48%/43% and 78%/75%/76%/76% respectively.
- [Client cohorts] Clients by account size moved from FY 24-25 to FY 25-26 as >$15mn 8 to 5, >$10mn 9 to 8, >$5mn 18 to 21, >$1mn 70 to 73.
- [Exceptional items] Adjusted PAT reconciliation adds back an Exceptional Item of ₹1,358.7 mn for twelve months ended 31.03.2026 (₹184.5 mn for 31.03.2025), with a tax impact of ₹166.9 mn; reported PAT for FY ended 31.03.2026 is ₹2,569.4 mn vs Adjusted PAT ₹3,761.2 mn.
- [Risk disclosure] Safe-harbour section flags dependence on clients in the United States of America, competition in CPaaS globally, and industry segment concentration among key risks.
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: Route Mobile Limited offers a scalable Omnichannel CPaaS/CXPaaS stack covering Enhanced Business Messaging, A2P Messaging, Roubot, OCEAN, Voice, Email, and Digital Identity and Authentication solutions for global enterprise clients, including several Fortune Global 500 companies. It also sells SMS filtering, analytics, SMS firewall, SMSC, MMSC and SMS monetization solutions to mobile network operators globally. Established in 2004 and headquartered in Mumbai, it serves more than 40,000 customers with operations in over 20 countries across Asia Pacific, the Middle East, Africa, Europe and the Americas.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Messaging:** A2P Messaging, 2-Way Messaging, FTEU Short Code, Route OTP, Route Connector, Mail2SMS, Number Lookup
- **Voice:** Voice Campaigns, Virtual Number, SIP Trunking, Missed Call, Click to Call, Safe Connect, CCaaS
- **Identity and verification:** Brandi5, Verified Messages, Verified Calls, Truecaller Verified Business Identity Solutions
- **Enhanced business messaging:** RCS Business Messaging, WhatsApp Business Platform, Viber Business Messages, Google Business Messages, Acculync, Facebook Messenger for Business, Telegram for Business
- **Contact Center-as-a-Service:** CCaaS cloud contact centre platform
- **Mobile operator solutions:** A2P SMS and voice firewalls, Intelligent filtering, Analytics, SMSC, MMSC, Monetization platforms, 365guard
- **Digital identity and security:** Fraud detection, Anti-phishing, Silent verification, SIM swap detection, Device location verification, Konera Network API-enriched solutions

latest_quarter.body: Gross Margin expanded to 22.9% FY26 (from 20.8%) and 23.3% in Q4 due to exit of low-margin ILD and domestic mix shift. EBITDA margin improved to 11.9% driven by operating leverage and cost initiatives; OPEX constrained mainly to wage indexation.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: Mid-to-high single digits for FY27; EBITDA Margin: ~12%; Order Inflow: Strong pipeline for MNO Firewall & Network APIs; Capex: Disciplined, focused on capability-led M&A rather than heavy infrastructure.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Pipeline described as 'strong' for AI-driven A2P SMS/Voice firewall solutions and Network API deployments (e.g., Claro deal live); specific monetary value not quantified but cited as key future revenue driver alongside cross-sell with BICS/Telesign.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Cross-sell into 3,100+ existing single-channel clients; Geographic expansion into Mexico/Philippines; US market entry via Telesign; 'India as Innovation Hub' model (e.g., Aakash Education proof point) scaled globally via Proximus; Bolt-on M&A for AI capabilities.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Expand the AI-first platform and embed AI across the customer engagement stack, using best available AI technologies rather than building foundational models in-house
- Deepen leadership in Network APIs and Digital Identity, scaling the Konera Network API Platform after transitioning it from experimentation to execution with integrations from major operators
- Accelerate innovation across omnichannel customer engagement and grow enterprise presence across India and international markets
- Improve operating efficiency and sustain profitable growth through disciplined execution
- Use India as the innovation engine: engineering teams design, develop and validate products in India for deployment across international markets, supported by a new technology hub in Hyderabad for AI, product engineering and Network APIs
- Run the Konera Strategic Expansion Plan out of India, where new capabilities are developed, pressure-tested with customers and cybersecurity partners, and refined before wider global deployment
- Leverage the Proximus Global combination with BICS and Telesign to cross-sell and expand reach across Europe, North America and other strategic markets
- The Company maintains a board-adopted Dividend Distribution Policy alongside its other corporate policies (published on the Company website), and the Board has placed a dividend on equity shares for the financial year ended March 31, 2026 before members for approval as ordinary business at the 22nd AGM. Governance framework: a six-member Board as on March 31, 2026 with one Executive Director/MD and five Non-Executive Directors including three Independent Directors, a Non-Executive and Non-Independent Chairman with the roles of Chairman, MD and CEO held by different individuals, and Board committees covering audit and internal controls, financial reporting, risk management, nomination and remuneration and CSR. All related party transactions are conducted under Audit Committee scrutiny on an arm's-length basis in the ordinary course of business, and the Company reports no material unlisted Indian subsidiaries during FY 2025-26. Statutory auditors M S K A & Associates LLP have been recommended for appointment for five years in place of the retiring auditors; the FY 2025-26 Auditors' Report and the Secretarial Audit Report carry no qualifications, reservations or adverse remarks, and there was no modified audit opinion.
- Scope 2 emissions of 171.37 metric tons of CO2 equivalent in the year, a total reduction of 17.58 metric tons of CO2 versus the previous year, achieved through dedicated energy optimization including efficient HVAC systems and LED lighting across facilities
- Water consumption of 3722.84 KL managed responsibly during the year
- Waste initiatives eliminated single-use plastics and established comprehensive e-waste recycling programmes
- Forward commitment to enhanced climate action through continued emissions reduction and renewable energy adoption, plus implementation of circular economy principles in operations
- CSR investment of INR 2.36 crores in community programmes focused on healthcare, education and elder care, with the CSR Committee chaired by Independent Director Mrs. Harita Gupta
- Certified quality management system complying with ISO 9001:2015 and information security management system complying with ISO/IEC 27001:2022 (certified by KVQA Certification Services Private Limited); ISO/IEC 27001:2022 surveillance was conducted during the year
- Board-level ESG oversight with 50% independent directors and zero tolerance for bribery and corruption; sustainability issues overseen through the Nomination & Remuneration, CSR and Risk Management Committees, with Managing Director Mr. Rajdipkumar Gupta the highest authority for the Business Responsibility policies
- Risk management systems established across all markets include climate-related risks
- The Company states it has set no specific ESG commitments, goals or targets with defined timelines, identifying only goals complementing its core business and its CSR programme in healthcare, education and sports
- NGRBC policies cover eight of the nine principles (P7 public advocacy has no dedicated policy) and extend to value chain partners through the ESG policy, Anti-Fraud/Anti-Bribery & Anti-Corruption Policy, Supplier Code of Conduct, POSH policy, insider trading code and Data Protection Policy
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Route Mobile is an asset-light CPaaS business and the annual report describes expansion as platform build-out, capability addition and inorganic activity rather than physical capacity. Strategic Pillar 01 ('Elevating the platform') sets out broadening beyond traditional messaging into a full customer-engagement ecosystem: expanding omnichannel engagement across WhatsApp, RCS, voice and other digital channels through the OCEAN platform; embedding AI and GenAI into engagement workflows including conversational interfaces, enterprise integrations and intelligent automation; and developing Network API and firewall solutions that use telecom infrastructure for identity verification, fraud prevention and secure digital interactions. Pillar 02 ('Accelerating AI-led innovation') makes India the Group's innovation hub, where new capabilities are developed, tested and scaled for global deployment, including building GenAI-native engagement solutions across chat, voice and messaging, deploying AI across engineering, testing, customer support and operational workflows, and scaling India-built Network API innovations across the global Proximus ecosystem. Pillar 04 ('Driving growth through partnerships and M&A') covers evaluating acquisitions in conversational AI, chatbot technologies and adjacent CPaaS capabilities, partnerships for faster entry into priority geographies and industry segments, collaboration with ISVs, telecom operators and technology partners, and cross-selling across the Proximus Global portfolio including BICS and Telesign. Pillar 03 focuses on deepening relationships within a base of more than 3,100 enterprise customers. The BRSR states that R&D and capex investments in specific technologies to improve environmental and social impacts were 'None', as the nature of the business does not involve material carbon emission or other pollutant. No rupee capex quantum is disclosed anywhere in this bundle.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Changing business composition moderated revenue alongside lower-margin international A2P SMS volumes, while profitability improved through product mix optimization, operational efficiencies and increasing contribution from higher-value solutions
- Enterprise demand is shifting from app-based interactions toward autonomous resolution, with Agentic AI able to reason, decide and execute multi-step actions across systems - management sees the combination of intelligence, trust and seamless execution becoming a defining competitive advantage
- AI capability expansion is expected to lift customer satisfaction: multilingual AI now supports more than 50 languages and intelligent flow detection reduces customer service resolution times by as much as 75%
- Network API integrations on the Konera Platform created a new stack of enterprise solutions, unlocked new revenue streams and established a unique positioning in the evolving market
- New products revenue of INR 3,526 Mn in FY 25-26, up 11.3% Y-o-Y, from intelligent industry-specific solutions across AI automation and omnichannel customer experience
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Route Mobile has structurally reset its business by exiting low-margin ILD volumes

open.item: The Company commits to deploying excess capital in a way that balances strategic investment in growth with meaningful returns to shareholders.
Capital will be directed at capability-led bolt-on acquisitions that expand the platform, enhance enterprise solution stickiness and accelerate entry into adjacent growth areas.
The Company will keep investing in AI-powered customer engagement, platform innovation, digital identity, Network APIs and next-generation communication technologies.

The Company will continue expanding its AI-first platform, deepen leadership in Network APIs and Digital Identity, accelerate omnichannel engagement innovation and grow enterprise presence across India and international markets.
Management remains committed to improving operating efficiency and sustaining profitable growth through disciplined execution.

The Company will broaden platform capabilities by expanding omnichannel engagement across WhatsApp, RCS, voice and other digital channels through its OCEAN platform and by embedding AI/GenAI into customer engagement workflows.

The Company will develop Network API and firewall solutions leveraging telecom infrastructure for identity verification, fraud prevention and secure digital interactions, and scale Network API innovations developed in India across the global Proximus ecosystem.

The Company is evaluating acquisitions in conversational AI, chatbot technologies and adjacent CPaaS capabilities, and pursuing partnerships that support faster entry into priority geographies and industry segments.
